\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Tensorization}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Bobkov.Tensorization
\section{Overview}
An extended Bobkov functional includes arbitrary additional coordinate functions alongside the discrete gradient. Symmetric pair contraction tensorizes, yielding contraction under simultaneous noise in all coordinates.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Extended profile-gradient functional]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.extendedFunctional}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.derivative, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p021-b001}
For $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ of real functions on the cube, write $V(f,g)(x)=(D_1f(x),\ldots,D_nf(x),g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x))$ and $F_P(f,g)=\mathbb E\sqrt{P(f)^2+\|V(f,g)\|_2^2}$, with $D_i$ the coordinate half-difference. The extended functional is $F_P(f,g)$ for arbitrary $n,m\ge0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gradient and additional coordinate vector]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.lengthVector}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.derivative}
For $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, $m\ge0$, and real cube functions $g_1,\ldots,g_m$, define $V(f,g)(x)=(D_1f(x),\ldots,D_nf(x),g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x))$, where $D_i$ is the coordinate half-difference.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Squared length decomposition]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.sum_sq_lengthVector}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.lengthVector, BooleanAnalysis.derivative}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a Boolean function, let
$g_1,\ldots,g_m:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. If
$V(f,g)(x)=(D_1f(x),\ldots,D_nf(x),g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x))$, where $D_i$ is the coordinate
half-difference, then
$\sum_{j=1}^{n+m}V(f,g)(x)_j^2=\sum_{i=1}^n(D_if(x))^2+\sum_{j=1}^m g_j(x)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Length under last-coordinate restriction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.extended_length_snoc}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.lengthVector, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.sum_sq_lengthVector, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.sum_sq_derivative_snoc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.derivative}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers, let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, let $f$ be a
real-valued function on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$, and let $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ be real-valued
functions on that cube. For every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and bit $b$, the square root of
$P(f(x,b))^2$, plus the sum of the squares of all coordinate derivatives of $f$ at
$(x,b)$ and the squares of all $g_j(x,b)$, equals the square root of
$P(f_b(x))^2+(D_{n+1}f(x,b))^2$ plus the squared length of the vector consisting of the
first $n$ derivatives of $f_b$ and the values of the restrictions $(g_j)_b$ at $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Linearity of the combined vector]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.lengthVector_linear_combination}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.lengthVector, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.derivative_linear_combination}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers, let $f_1,f_2:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $g_1,g_2$ be
$m$-tuples of real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^n$, let $c,d\in\mathbb R$, and let
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$. The combined vector of the linear combinations $cf_1+df_2$ and
$cg_1+dg_2$ at $x$ is $c$ times the combined vector of $(f_1,g_1)$ at $x$ plus $d$ times
the combined vector of $(f_2,g_2)$ at $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise and last-coordinate restriction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.lengthVector_noise_restriction}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.lengthVector, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.lengthVector_linear_combination, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noiseOp_restrictLast_eq_fun, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, let $f$ be a real-valued
function on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$, let $g$ be an $m$-tuple of such functions, and let
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$. The combined vector formed from the noise-operator
images of the restrictions of $f$ and $g$ at $b$, evaluated at $x$, equals the combined
vector formed from the noise-operator images of their last-coordinate averages, plus
$\sigma(b)$ times the combined vector formed from the noise-operator images of their
last-coordinate half-differences.
\end{lemma}

$b\in\{0,1\}$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. The combined vector of the restrictions at $b$ of the

half-differences at $x$.
\end{lemma}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.extendedFunctional_restrictLast}

Let $n,m\ge0$, let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, and let $f,g_1,\ldots,g_m$ be real-valued
functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. If $f_0,f_1$ and $g_{j,0},g_{j,1}$ denote their
restrictions to the last coordinate and $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, then $F_P(f,(g_j)_j)$ equals
$\bigl(F_P(f_0,(d_f,g_{j,0})_j)+F_P(f_1,(d_f,g_{j,1})_j)\bigr)/2$.
\end{lemma}

Let $n,m\ge0$, $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and let $f,g_1,\ldots,g_m$
be real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. Write $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$ and
$d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and define $a_{g_j},d_{g_j}$ in the same way from the last-coordinate
restrictions. Then $F_P(T_\rho f,(T_\rho g_j)_j)$ equals the uniform expectation over
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$ of $L(\rho,c(x))$, with first argument $T_\rho a_f(x)$, second argument
$T_\rho d_f(x)$, vector arguments $V(T_\rho a_f,(T_\rho a_{g_j})_j)(x)$ and $V(T_\rho
d_f,(T_\rho d_{g_j})_j)(x)$, and $c(x)=(\rho T_\rho d_f(x))^2$.
\end{lemma}

\leanok

Let $n,m\ge0$, let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and let $f$ and
$g_1,\ldots,g_m$ be real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. Write $f_0,f_1$ and
$g_{j,0},g_{j,1}$ for their restrictions to the last coordinate, and put
$a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, with $a_{g_j}=(g_{j,0}+g_{j,1})/2$ and
$d_{g_j}=(g_{j,0}-g_{j,1})/2$. Then the uniform-cube expectation of $L(1,B(x)^2)$, where
$B=T_\rho d_f(x)$, the first argument of $L$ is $A=T_\rho a_f(x)$, and its vector
arguments are $U=V(T_\rho a_f,(T_\rho a_{g_j})_j)(x)$ and $W=V(T_\rho d_f,(T_\rho
d_{g_j})_j)(x)$, equals the average of $F_P$ on the two last-coordinate restrictions:
$\bigl(F_P(T_\rho f_0,(T_\rho d_f,T_\rho g_{0})) + F_P(T_\rho f_1,(T_\rho d_f,T_\rho
g_{1}))\bigr)/2$. Here $T_\rho$ is the Fourier noise operator, $V$ consists of the
coordinate half-differences followed by the listed additional coordinates, and $F_P$ is
the uniform expectation of the square root of $P$ of the function squared plus the
squared Euclidean length of $V$.
\end{lemma}

Let $n,m\ge0$ and $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous on $[0,1]$ and nonnegative
there. Suppose that whenever $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$,
$P(a)\le\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{P(a-b)^2+b^2}\bigr)/2$. For any real-valued
functions $f,g_1,\ldots,g_m$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ with $f(x)\in[0,1]$ for every $x$, and any
$\rho\in[0,1]$, the extended functional satisfies $F_P(T_\rho f,(T_\rho g_j)_j)\le
F_P(f,(g_j)_j)$, where $T_\rho$ is the Fourier noise operator.
\end{lemma}
